events.title: Update#5: State of the game
events.summary: Greetings!What’s New Since the Demo Launch?After fixing the most frustrating issues in the Steel Wolverines demo, it’s time to build the missing mechanics and develop features that have so far been placeholders. Here are some of the changes I’ve already made:1. MANPADS, shotguns, and dronesShoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles such as the Stinger are no longer a way to counter small FPV drones. I’ve also added shotguns that infantry can carry. They work much like active protection systems (APS)

events.title: Update#4: Demo - Quality of Life Update
events.summary: Hello,I’d describe the response to the demo as positive :) Many of you seem to understand that Steel Wolverines is trying to combine classic ideas from 1990s games with modern UI/UX expectations and the realities of today’s battlefield, which go far beyond the concepts associated with era of Operation Desert Storm. Keep in mind that what you're seeing is still an alpha version that contains bugs and errors/compromises in terms of realism, which should be corrected over time.Demo Quality of Life

events.title: Update#1: Demo status and content
events.summary: Greetings!Steel Wolverines is wrapping up its 8th month of development. With Skirmish Mode working satisfactorily, the campaign improving (kind of), and the map editor functioning properly, the main focus has now shifted toward releasing the demo.First Demo Content — ETA: SeptemberThe first demo release is planned for the first two weeks of September.The demo will feature one meeting engagement scenario on a map based on Zubriai, Lithuania, playable as NATO.
